text:
nora_fin: Flagging an anomaly: several AWS Marketplace invoices show unexpectedly high prorated amounts for customers who changed tiers mid-billing-cycle. Looks like the proration multiplier applied twice for the same hourly window.

sam.billing: Can you paste an example invoice line?

nora_fin: Sure. From export: ```invoice_id,sku,customer_id,plan,period_start,period_end,units,unit_price,proration_factor,amount
aws-2026-05-10-201,ml-infer,acct-5543,pro->enterprise,2026-05-10T00:00Z,2026-05-15T12:00Z,120,0.50,2.0,120.00``` The amount seems off: 120 units * $0.50 * 2.0 = $120, but the expected proration factor should have been 1.25 for the partial window, not 2.0.

ashley_partners: Partners reported a UI change where they now submit both the old and new plan rows during a tier change; our ingestion may be double-counting the overlap if both rows are tagged and we also apply a proration adjustment.

ingestbot: Ingest log shows entries: "accepted line: plan_change_old_row" and then "accepted line: plan_change_new_row" and later "applied proration_adjustment for change id 9f3a". The adjustment step didn't dedupe by change id.

margo_sre: Sounds like a logic bug in the proration state machine. Hotfix idea: when a plan change pair arrives, prefer canonicalized single-window calculation (split the billing window once) instead of applying per-row proration + global adjustment. We can detect pairs by identical customer_id + adjacent timestamps + a shared change_id header when present.

sam.billing: Operationally we need two things: 1) fix ingestion to avoid double-prorating for already paired rows, and 2) run a reconciliation job to identify affected invoices and issue corrective credits.

nora_fin: Agreed. I'll need a CSV of affected invoice_ids for accounting so we can generate credit memos.

margo_sre: I'll open a branch and a small schema change: if header `x-change-id` present, mark group and skip the later proration_adjustment. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/501 (includes unit tests and rollout notes). ETA 2h for code + staged canary.

ashley_partners: Quick ask for partner comms: can we provide a mapping of affected invoice IDs and an explanation template? Some partners are already asking why customers got charged more.

sam.billing: I created a query to surface candidates: SELECT invoice_id FROM marketplace_export WHERE marketplace='aws' AND proration_factor>1.5 AND period_start BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-05-15'; Exported file: gs://billing-exports/2026-05/proration-issues-may10.csv.

invoicebot: Automation: queued job rc-20260510-prorate-fix to reprocess candidate files after hotfix. Job id rc-20260510-99.

nora_fin: After scoping, 57 invoice lines across 34 invoices appear impacted. We'll prepare credit memos for 34 customers; estimated credit total ~$3,420.

margo_sre: Hotfix deployed to staging and canarying on 5% traffic. No new regressions in the metrics. Rolling to prod in 30 minutes with feature flag.

sam.billing: Reprocessing run scheduled after prod rollout. Finance ops: please hold any cash application for those invoices until credits are applied automatically.

ashley_partners: Partner message draft: "We detected a reporting/format change that caused double proration for a subset of mid-cycle plan changes. We're issuing corrective credits and have patched our ingestion to prevent recurrence. Full invoice list attached." I'll drop the draft in the partner tracker.

nora_fin: Good work. Post-mortem actions: 1) add unit tests around change_id grouping and proration; 2) add a Redwood Console guardrail: if proration_factor >1.5 for any row, create a high-severity billing alert; 3) add partner onboarding note about sending a single change_id header on plan changes.

margo_sre: Adding tests and dashboard updates to the PR. Will update ops runbook with rollback steps.

invoicebot: Reprocess complete: rc-20260510-99 finished; 52 lines corrected, 5 require partner confirmation. Credits generated for 29 invoices; queued manual review for 5.

nora_fin: Closing loop for now. Finance will reconcile in the month-end close. If partners dispute any of the five, we'll escalate. Thanks everyone.
